frontMatter.welcome:
Dear Colleagues,
It is indeed a privilege to have you as a member of our ALCHEM family.
It gives us immense pleasure to share this booklet containing the essence of our HR, Legal & other Management Policies.
“Alchem‘s Handbook of Policies” provides us with an opportunity to learn about our various HR, Legal & other Management Policies and enhance our understanding of these policies.
This Employee Handbook applies to all business units, departments, and operational functions of Alchem International Pvt. Ltd. It serves as a unified reference document outlining the company’s expectations, policies, procedures, values, and standards of conduct for all personnel associated with the organization.

- Manufacturing, Production & Processing Units
- Botanical Raw Material Sourcing & Primary Operations
- Extraction, Purification & Distillation Facilities
- Research & Development (R&D) Centres
- Quality Control (QC) and Quality Assurance (QA)
- Regulatory Affairs, Documentation & Compliance
- Environmental Health, Safety & Sustainability (EHS)
- Procurement, Supply Chain & Inventory Management
- Human Resources, Training & Administrative Services
- Engineering, Utilities & Maintenance
- Sales, Commercial, and Customer Support Operations
- Warehouse, Storage & Packaging Units
The policies and guidelines outlined in this handbook apply to:
- Permanent employees
- Contract and agency workers
- Trainees and interns
- Apprentices
- Consultants and technical experts working on-site
- Third-party service providers and outsourced staff engaged in Alchem operations

Alchem condemns all forms of exploitation of children. Alchem will not recruit child labours and supports the elimination of exploitive child labour.
The International Labour organisation (ILO) uses term ‘child labour’ to cover all economic activities carried out by person less than eighteen years of age regardless of their occupational status (wage earners, own account workers etc.) but not house hold work performed by them in their parent’s home except where such work can be assimilated to economic activity as for example, when a child must devote his or her entire time to work so that his or her parents can be employed outside the home, and is therefore, deprived of the possibility of going to school.
- This Standard operating procedure incorporates all procedures to prohibit any kind of child labour practices within its premises, offices, factories or warehouses.

chapters.title: Prevention Of Sexual Harassment At Workplace
chapters.text:
## OBJECTIVE
- Sexual Harassment by its very nature is a form of misconduct that gravely undermines the employment relationship. By framing the Anti-Sexual Harassment Policy (“POSH” or “Policy”), Alchem International Pvt. Ltd. (“Company”) endeavours to prohibit, prevent and deter the commission of acts of Sexual Harassment at the Workplace and provide a procedure for redressal of complaints pertaining to such incidences. Employees of the Company who violate this policy will be subjected to strict disciplinary proceedings.
- POSH sets out the types of behaviour that are unacceptable, the forms of redressal available against such behaviour and the action to be taken if a false complaint has been filed. In circumstances where the issue can be resolved at an early stage, the Company will promote conciliation between the Complainant (“Aggrieved” or “Victim”) and the Respondent/ Harasser (accused of act(s) of Sexual Harassment). However, where the issue is serious and persistent, a complaint or report of Sexual Harassment will be investigated immediately, and appropriate action will be taken against the Respondent. Such action will depend upon the nature and gravity of the offence.
## SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY
- This Policy is applicable upon all the Employees of the Company whether hired directly or indirectly at its Workplace or during the course of employment. This policy shall also apply to all visitors who arrive at the Company’s premises. The copy of policy is explained and given at the time of employment. And for reference, this Policy is also available on with HR/admin departments for information and compliance by Employees of the Company.
- Workplace includes:
- All offices or other premises where activities in relation to the Company’s business are undertaken or conducted.
- Any place visited by an Employee of the Company arising out of or during the course of his/her employment, including transportation provided by the Company, if any, for undertaking such journey.
- Where Sexual Harassment occurs as a result of an act or omission by any third party or outsider, the Company will take all necessary and reasonable steps to assist the aggrieved person in terms of support and preventive action, as per the provisions of applicable law.
- Sexual Harassment may be one or a series of incidents involving unsolicited and unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favours, or any other verbal or physical conduct of sexual nature. Sexual Harassment at Workplace shall include, any unwelcome sexually determined behaviour (whether directly or by implication) as:
- Physical contact and advances; or
- A demand or request for sexual favour; or
- Sexually coloured remarks; or
- Showing pornography; or
- Threat or innuendoes, touching, patting, pinching; or
- Comments about physical appearance; or
- Obscene email, SMS, MMS, messages, phonographic or sexually oriented jokes etc; or
- Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct/act of a sexual nature; or
- Any conduct that has the purpose or the effect of interfering with an individual’s work performance or creating an intimidating, offensive or hostile environment or rendering of humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety or implied or explicit promise of preferential or detrimental treatment in his / her Association.
- Capitalized terms used herein and not defined herein shall have the meaning ascribed to such term in The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”).
## NTERNAL COMPLAINTS COMMITTEE
3.1 Constitution of Internal Complaints Committee
3.1.1 As per the provisions of the Act, the Company has constituted a Committee known as Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) for addressing complaints relating to Sexual Harassment.
3.1.2 If a complaint is registered against any member of the ICC, then that member will be replaced by a new member. Such new member will be appointed by the Company.
3.1.3 The Details of the ICC members are mentioned in the Annexure – 1 to this Policy.
## REDRESSAL PROCESS
- The Company is committed to provide a supportive and compassionate environment to resolve concerns of Sexual Harassment. Any such issues/ complaints can be resolved under the process given herein under.
- Informal Resolution:
- When an incident of Sexual Harassment occurs, the Victim needs to communicate their disapproval or objections immediately to the Harasser and request the Harasser to refrain from such activities and behave decently. If the harassment does not stop or if the Victim is not comfortable addressing the Harasser directly, the Victim can bring their concern(s) to the attention of the Supervisor, the Human Resource (“HR”) Team, or to the ICC for redressal of their grievances. The ICC will thereafter provide advice or extend support to solve the matter informally.
- Formal Resolution

chapters.title: Confidentiality
chapters.text:
- The Company understands that it is difficult for the Victim to come forward with a complaint of Sexual Harassment and recognizes the interest of the Victim in preserving the confidentiality of the matter.
- Confidentiality will be maintained throughout the investigatory process to the extent practicable and appropriate under the circumstances. Publication, communication or giving information to public and media of contents of the complaint, identity and addresses of the complainant, Respondent and witnesses, information related to conciliation or enquiry proceedings, recommendations by the ICC, and action taken by the Company is treated as confidential and thereof as a consequence prohibited.
- However, in order to disseminate information regarding the justice done to the Complainant, the Company under this Policy can publish data without disclosing name, address, identity, or any other particulars leading to identification of the persons involved.
- The Company, apart from other disciplinary actions shall also recover a sum of INR 50,000/- (Fifty Thousand) as penalty and/or the actual losses and damages occurred, whichever is higher, from any Employee of the Company who violates the confidentiality obligation under this policy.
## DISSEMINATION OF THE POLICY
7.1 A copy of this Policy shall be made available to all the Employees of the Company and to all new recruits and they shall sign a statement acknowledging that they have received, read, understood and will abide by the Policy.
## POLICY REVIEW AND MODIFICATION
8.1 This Policy can be amended / modified / withdrawn at any point of time without any notice, at the discretion of the Management.

- All the members and Presiding Officer of the ICC shall remain its member for a maximum period of three years. In case, any member or Presiding Officer elects to resign from his/her post, he/she shall give prior notice of 1 (one) month in writing stating the reason for the same.

chapters.title: Mobile Phone Policy
chapters.text:
## General
1. Our cell phone Policy outlines guidelines for usage of all phones at work. While it is recognised that all phones (especially smart phones) have become an integral part of our everyday life, their utility has to be balanced with certain other considerations at the workplace. Many of us are privy to sensitive company related information which is useful to our competitors. We are also vulnerable to certain personal and external pressures in our lives like offers of new jobs, better wages etc. Hence, the cell phone Policy being outlined in the succeeding paras is not a ‘restriction’ but a ‘work ethic’ that we must religiously follow at our work-place, particularly in factories.
All important functionaries have access to the computer and the internet at the workplace. On the other hand, photography is required to be restricted for obvious reasons. Justifying requirement of smart phones for casual photography of products, brochures, machinery or locations is inappropriate. Hence in our factories, smart phones require to be restricted for usage only within the senior officials of the Company.
## Photography
Each factory will purchase one simple digital camera (in case not possessing one) for essential photography which will be carried out only under appropriate supervision. The same will be kept under lock and key at appropriate locations in factories, preferably with the EHS dept.
## General Policy
- The new mobile Policy will be applicable from 05 Nov 18. The mobile replacement Policy will be applicable to Dy. Managers and above and selected STLs/ Asst. Managers. Remainder staff, where considered essential will continue under the old Policy and company will purchase phones for them on “as required basis.” List of person’s holding company phones / Sims as also those eligible under the new Mobile Replacement Policy are enclosed as Appendix. A (BLB), Appendix B (NMR), Appendix C (Alchem), Appendix D (HO) & Appendix E (Phyto). The contents of these Appendices are, however, dynamic in nature and will change from time to time depending upon accretion/reduction of Staff. Such changes, however, will only be executed with approval of HR, BLB as per procedure laid down in subsequent paras.
- Life of a mobile phone will be presumed to be 3 years. During the life time of the mobile, all costs of maintenance /repair, if needed, will be borne by the user. In case the mobile set is lost/ damaged beyond economical repair before its life is over, the pro-rata cost of balance period (balance amount calculated after subtracting 3 per cent depreciation every month) shall be recovered from the employee and he can buy a new mobile set.
- In case of separation, 3% depreciation per month will be considered and the balance amount shall be recovered from the employee.
- Initial purchase of new mobile sets will be based on the serviceability of the previously issued set and not just the three year period. Further, old android/basic phones available with the HR Dept. will be first utilized before moving on to the new mobile replacement Policy. Hence, although the new mobile Policy commences on 05 Nov 18, actual movement into the 3 year replacement cycle may be gradual in certain cases. However, after the new purchase of a mobile set, an employee can replace his set after 3 years for all subsequent replacements.
- In general, for factories, smart phones will be authorised to Senior Managers and above. Others will be provided non-internet basic phones.
- At HO Sultanpur (including Phyto), possession of mobile phones will be designation based and there are no restrictions on the type of phone being carried. However, persons below Asst. Manager level will not be covered under the new mobile replacement Policy and provision of phones to them will be “need based”.

chapters.title: Flexible Work Arrangements
chapters.text:
To support employees with caregiving responsibilities or family commitments, the Company may provide:
- Adjusted work timings or short-term schedule flexibility
- Permission-based early departure or late arrival when needed
- Temporary role adjustments for employees returning from parental or long-term caregiving leave
- Consideration of workload distribution to reduce stress during critical family situations
Supervisors are encouraged to evaluate such requests with empathy while maintaining operational needs.
## Return-to-Work Support
Employees returning from extended maternity, paternity, or caregiving leave may receive:
- Gradual reintegration support
- Temporary workload modifications
- Clear guidance from HR on transitioning back into regular duties
- Encouragement to discuss any challenges related to balancing work and family responsibilities
This ensures a smooth and dignified return to the workplace.
## Support for Employees with Special-Needs or Elderly Dependents
The Company recognizes that caregiving extends beyond childcare. Employees caring for family members with disabilities, cognitive impairments, or chronic medical conditions may request:
- Flexible timing
- Additional permission for medical appointments
- HR assistance in accessing government schemes or documentation
- Priority in emergency leave approvals
## Psychological Well-Being and Family Stress Support
- Employees facing emotional or psychological strain due to caregiving pressures may reach out to HR for confidential support or guidance.
- Awareness programs may be conducted to address stress management, family/work balance, and wellness.
- Supervisors are trained to respond sensitively to employees facing family-related stress or burnout.
## Family Engagement and Workplace Community
To foster a sense of belonging and support, the Company may organize:
- Family day events
- Health camps open to employees’ families
- Awareness drives on health, hygiene, and nutrition
- Volunteer programs that include employee families
Such initiatives strengthen bonds between employees, their families, and the workplace community.
## Inclusive Approach to All Family Structures
Alchem’s family-friendly support applies equally to:
- Single parents
- Adoptive or foster parents
- Guardianship arrangements
- Employees caring for non-biological dependents
- Same-household dependent care scenarios
This ensures fairness and equal opportunity for all employees, regardless of family circumstances.
## Continuous Improvement
The Company periodically reviews its family-friendly measures to ensure alignment with evolving employee needs, labour laws, and industry best practices. Feedback from employees is encouraged and incorporated to enhance support programs and strengthen long-term employee well-being.
## Transparent Communication of Compensation Structure
Alchem International Private Limited is committed to maintaining a fair, consistent, and transparent remuneration system that employees can clearly understand. To ensure that all employees not only HR personnel are informed about how their compensation is structured, reviewed, and progressed, the Company has established a clear communication framework covering salary components, pay progression, bonus eligibility, and remuneration-related policies. This promotes trust, eliminates ambiguity, and empowers employees with clarity regarding their present and future compensation.
## Communication of Salary Components
Upon joining the Company, all employees receive a formal Appointment Letter and Salary Structure that clearly outline:
- Basic salary
- Allowances (HRA, conveyance, special allowance, etc.)
- Statutory contributions (PF, ESI, gratuity)
- Deductions, if applicable
- Gross and net compensation
This ensures transparency and helps employees understand each element of their remuneration package.
Employees also receive a monthly salary slip providing a detailed breakdown of earnings and deductions for ongoing clarity.
## Induction Briefing on Compensation Practices
During onboarding, HR conducts a structured orientation where employees are briefed on:
- How salaries are determined
- Applicable wage and social security laws
- Bonus and incentive eligibility
- Allowances and benefits
- Overtime pay rules and statutory entitlements
Employees may ask questions or seek clarifications at any time to ensure full understanding of the remuneration framework.
## Annual Salary Review Communication
During the annual appraisal cycle, the Company communicates:
- Criteria influencing salary revisions
- Linkage between performance evaluation and compensation
- Market considerations and internal salary benchmarks
- Effective dates and mechanisms of revision
Revised salary letters are issued individually to employees, ensuring complete transparency regarding changes in remuneration.
## Communication of Bonus and Incentive Schemes
The Company provides clear communication to eligible employees about:
- Bonus calculation rules

chapters.title: Employee Communication and Transparency
chapters.text:
Employees are informed of:
- Wage components
- Allowances
- Revisions or increments
- Applicable statutory contributions and entitlements
HR maintains an open channel for employees to raise concerns regarding wage adequacy, discrepancies, or financial well-being.
## Continuous Improvement and Monitoring
The Company periodically evaluates the effectiveness of its wage adequacy framework and implements improvements where required. This includes:
- Reviewing internal processes for accuracy and fairness
- Monitoring external changes that may impact wage adequacy
- Updating compensation strategies based on organizational needs and employee feedback
## Employee Development and Mobility System
Alchem International Private Limited is committed to fostering an environment that encourages continuous learning, career advancement, and internal growth. To support the professional development of employees and ensure optimal utilization of internal talent, the Company promotes structured internal mobility across all levels and functions. Internal mobility helps employees grow within the organization and enables the Company to retain skilled talent while building a versatile workforce.
## Vertical Mobility (Promotions & Advancement)
Employees demonstrating strong performance, skill advancement, leadership potential, and alignment with organizational values may be considered for promotion to higher-level roles. Promotions are based on transparent criteria, including performance evaluations, competency assessments, and organizational requirements.
## Horizontal Mobility (Cross-Department Transfers)
Employees may apply for movement to other departments or functions at the same job level to expand their knowledge, gain diverse experience, or align their career interests with emerging opportunities. Such moves support skill diversification and broaden organizational capability.
## Geographical Mobility (Inter-Location Opportunities)
Where feasible, employees may be offered opportunities to work at different company locations to support expansion activities, enhance operational knowledge, or contribute to specific projects. These assignments help employees develop adaptability and broaden their exposure to different operational environments.
## Transversal Mobility (Cross-Skilling & Role Transitions)
Employees may progress across functions or roles by leveraging transferable skills, specialized training, or cross-functional exposure. The Company supports cross-skilling initiatives that allow employees to expand their technical and managerial competencies and transition to roles that match their evolving capabilities.

chapters.title: Internal Job Posting & Talent Identification
chapters.text:
Vacant positions are communicated internally to ensure employees are aware of available opportunities within the organization. Employees may apply for openings that align with their interests and competencies. Supervisors and HR jointly assess applications based on skill fit, performance history, and developmental potential.
## Job Rotation and Cross-Functional Exposure Programs
Where operationally appropriate, employees may be assigned temporary or rotational responsibilities across related functions. These assignments help employees gain broader business understanding and prepare them for future roles by strengthening functional depth and cross-functional collaboration.
## Job Shadowing and Mentorship Opportunities
Employees may participate in job shadowing or mentorship arrangements to enhance learning, observe senior roles, and acquire critical skills. These programs strengthen internal capability-building and support career growth pathways.
## Transparent Promotion & Transfer Procedures
All career progression decisions—including promotions, transfers, and role changes—are communicated clearly to employees. HR ensures that movement decisions are made fairly, consistently, and based on merit, performance, and organizational requirements.
## Individual Development Plans (IDPs)
Employees are encouraged to work with their supervisors to create Individual Development Plans, which help outline career aspirations, training needs, and readiness for internal mobility opportunities.
## Commitment to Employee Growth
The Company continuously evaluates its internal mobility practices and incorporates employee feedback to strengthen career development mechanisms. Through structured mobility pathways, Alchem aims to develop internal talent, support long-term career growth, and foster an engaged and future-ready workforce.
## WORKING HOURS & OVER TIME:
That as per Section 51 of the Factories Act 1948, No, Worker is allowed to work more than 9 Hours in a Day and 48 hours in a week.

chapters.title: Attendance:
chapters.text:
- The attendance is done via Biometric System. This attendance & online leave system shall be applicable to all the employees. It is essential for all the employees to mark their presence by punching twice a day – one while entering & the other while exiting company premises.
- The employee must apply online through HRM and intimate to the Time Office in case of Outdoor Duty (OD) by submitting the OD Authorization Form duly approved by the HOD. Generally, all such authorization shall reach the Time Office before the employee proceeds for outdoor duty.
- All employees are required to verify their or attendance, and if there is any discrepancy to notify to the Time Office immediately.
## Working Time Details:
[table]
| Shift | I | II | III | G |
| Shift Timings | 0600 Hrs to 1400 Hrs | 1400 Hrs to 2200 Hrs | 2200Hrs to 0600 Hrs | 0900 Hrs to 1 1700 Hrs |
| Weekly Off Change | Within Three days of Original Week Off and Three Days of Duty between Two Weekly |
Minimum Wages: Alchem compensates the employees with wages and benefits that meet or exceed the legally required minimum as per state government.
Alchem Takes Extra precaution while following the worker shift timings, which are 8 Hours and 30 Minutes (Including Lunch and Tea Break) or 8 hours (excluding Lunch or Tea Break), or Forty-Eight Hours in a week, to ensure its worker/employees are well rested and maintains proper work life balance. However, there may be certain conditions/circumstances which may arise due to work exigencies where a worker may be required to work extra hours/overtime, to tackle such circumstances the company will follow the below stated guidelines: -
Extra wages for overtime. — (1) Normally Alchem Allows, a worker works in a factory for more than 8.30 hours (Including Lunch and Tea Break) or 8 Hours (Excluding Lunch and Tea Break) in any day or for more than forty eight hours in any week.
In case the working hours exceeds the shift timings more than 8:30 hours (Including Lunch and Tea Break) or 8 Hours (Excluding Lunch and Tea Break) the Alchem will Pay, in respect of overtime work, wages at the rate of twice his ordinary rate of wages.
For the purposes of “ordinary rate of wages” means the basic wages plus such allowances, including the cash but does not include a bonus and wages for overtime work.
No worker is allowed to work more than 54 hours in any week at a stretch and the total number of hours including of overtime work hours.
Intervals for rest.— All workers in a factory each day are fixed in the manner that no period shall exceed five hours and that no worker shall work for more than five hours before he has had an interval for rest of at least half an hour.
All workers must be provided weekly off, and the manager shall ensure that weekly off is granted to every worker within maximum 10 days of working.
Prohibition of overlapping shifts. — The Shift timings of workman shall be so arranged that more than one relay of workers is engaged in work of the same kind at the same time. There will be minimum 16-hour rest before any change of shift of any workman, means no workman is allowed to work in Changed shift without mandatory rest of 16 hours.

chapters.title: Disciplinary Action
chapters.text:
Employees who violate this policy may face disciplinary consequences in proportion to their violation. HR will determine how serious an employee’s offense is and take the appropriate action:
For minor violations (e.g. bringing in personal visitors without authorization), employees may only receive verbal reprimands.
- For more serious violations (e.g. bringing in unauthorized visitors who rob or damage company property), employees may face severe disciplinary actions up to and including termination.
## EMPLOYEES COMPENSATION
## Employer Liability
An accident caused to an employee in the course of his employment the employer is liable to pay compensation in accordance with the Employees Compensation Act 1923 with various conditions of fulfilment. The compensation ceases to come into effect if the employee is found to be in contravention to the laid out rules as per the above act.
Alchem is committed to maintain the highest standard of transparency in judgment of any compensation payable & reporting the incident to the Factory Inspectorate / Labour department of the State.
## Amount of Compensation
Subject to provisions of this Act the amount of compensation payable to an employee in the case of
- Death from injury sustained during employment
- Permanent disablement resulting from injury
- Partial disablement
- Temporary disablement
Will be decided as per the provision of ECA 1923 & as per directives received from Factory Inspectorate / Labour Department after reporting of the accident.
Compensation will be paid as soom as it falls due as per the above Act.
Wages will be calculated based on the monthly wages which mean the amount of wages deemed to be able for a month’s service.
Alchem is already insuring its employees through a Group Accident Policy (GPA). In case of an accident permanent or partial injury caused to any employee resulting in death, disablement, temporary disablement during the course of his employment the accident will be reported & the compensation will be decided by the Third Party Assurance.
## Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Recruitment
## ntroduction
- This Policy incorporates all procedures and policies involving recruitment so as to ensure a fair, transparent and systematic process in hiring of new talent. The document also ensures that all recruitment activities are efficient and aligned with the company’s goals and legal requirements.
- The policy also allows for greater internal development as well as the opportunity for new and exciting talent to join the business.
## Purpose
- To streamline the Recruitment procedure by outlining the steps required to be undertaken to hire a new prospective employee with the right skills, knowledge and experience.
- To exercise overall manpower management and requisite controls in terms of number of employees and HR related costs / economics in line with current company policies.
## Responsibilities
- It shall be the responsibility of the HR & Administrative head of department to efficiently implement this policy and monitor / review its efficacy from time to time. Initial hiring of competent Recruitment Managers / Staff would be the key to efficient roll-out of this policy.
- The Recruiting Manager will be responsible to ensure that the recruitment process is strictly followed with emphasis on the following:-
- Clear Objectives To attract the best talent available in the market, promote diversity and ensure compliance with relevant labour laws.

- Effective Candidate Communication In that, ensure timely and respectful communication throughout the recruitment process including updates on progress towards final selection.
- Fair and unbiased evaluation and recommendations Should only be based on the job requirement and core competencies of the candidate so as to enable final and appropriate selection within the process.
- The Recruitment team will function under the direct supervision of the Recruitment Manager to ensure consistency in application of this policy. They will actively execute and provide support in conduct of recruitment activities within the overall framework of the Policy.

## The Geographic reach
The Act provides that the Company shall give preference to the local area and areas around it where it operates, for spending the amount earmarked for Corporate Social Responsibility. The Company will thus give preference to conducting CSR activities in the state of Haryana wherein the Company has/will have its operations. However, the Committee may identify such areas other than stated above, as it may deem fit, and recommend it to the Board for undertaking CSR activities.
## Budget Allocation
The total budget for the CSR projects will be recommended by the CSR Committee and approved by the Board as per the applicable rules, regulations of the Act as may be amended from time to time.
- The Company would spend not less than 2% of the average Net Profits of the Company made during the three immediately preceding financial years. The surplus arising out of the CSR activity will not be part of business profits of the Company. The Corpus would thus include the 2% of average net profits, as aforesaid, any income arising there from and surplus arising out of CSR activities.
- The Company may build CSR capacities of its personnel and/or those of its implementing agencies through Institutions with established track records of at least three financial years but such expenditure shall not exceed five percent of total CSR expenditure of the Company in one financial year.
- However if the Company ceases to be covered under sub-section (1) of Section 135 of the Act for three financial years, then it shall not be required to, comply with the provisions laid down under sub-section (2) to (5) of the said section, till such time it meets the criteria specified in sub-section (1) of the Act.
## Administration of CSR Projects
The Corporation can meet its CSR obligations by funneling its activities on its own or through a third party, such as a society, trust, foundation or Section 8 company (i.e., a company with charitable purposes) that has an established record of at least five years in CSR-like activities. Companies may also collaborate and pool their resources, which could be especially useful for small and medium-sized enterprises. The Head of the CSR
Committee will have the power to sanction any project for CSR up to a limit of 7.5 lakhs, above which Board ‘s approval will be required to sanction the amount.

chapters.title: Grievance Mechanism
chapters.text:
Alchem International Private Limited is committed to fostering a transparent, accountable, and respectful workplace where all employees feel safe to raise concerns without fear of retaliation. To support this commitment, the company maintains a comprehensive, company-wide grievance mechanism that enables all employees and associated stakeholders to report incidents, risks, or concerns related to workplace conditions, ethical conduct, and policy compliance.
This mechanism ensures that every individual—regardless of employment type, role, or location—has access to confidential, reliable, and responsive channels to report issues and seek redressal. The system is designed to identify, address, and remediate concerns promptly and fairly, enabling continuous improvement and compliance with legal and ethical standards.
## Scope of the Mechanism
The grievance mechanism applies to all permanent employees, contractual workers, trainees, apprentices, third-party workers, and business partners operating within Alchem’s facilities or supply chain.
Employees may raise concerns related to:
- Labour and human rights violations
- Forced or bonded labour
- Child labour or adolescent labour issues
- Discrimination of any kind
- Sexual harassment or other forms of harassment
- Workplace bullying, intimidation, or abuse of authority
- Wage or overtime discrepancies
- Delayed or incorrect payment of wages
- Excessive working hours or forced overtime
- Unsafe working conditions
- Lack of PPE or safety measures
- Workplace accidents or near-misses
- Environmental risks or unsafe disposal practices
- Ethical misconduct or violation of Code of Conduct
- Fraud, corruption, bribery, or facilitation payments
- Conflict of interest or misuse of company property
- Retaliation for raising a concern
- Breach of confidentiality
- Violation of company policies (HR, EHS, procurement, ethical business practices, etc.)
- Issues related to facilities (canteen, sanitation, drinking water, transport, housing)
- Interpersonal conflicts affecting dignity or work performance
- Contractor or third-party worker exploitation
- Inadequate implementation of legal or policy requirements
- Systemic issues that compromise safety, legality, ethics, or employee well-being
- Any other workplace-related incident, risk, or concern
## Reporting Channels
Alchem provides multiple accessible and confidential channels for submitting grievances:
- Written complaints to any member of the Complaint Redressal Committee (CRC)
- Email to: contact@alcheminternational.com
- Reporting to supervisors, HR representatives, or department heads
- Confidential submissions to the Ethics Committee for sensitive matters
- Direct reporting to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) for POSH cases
- Physical complaint boxes installed at specific locations
All channels ensure confidentiality and non-retaliation.
## Grievance Handling Process
## Step 1: Receipt & Acknowledgement
- Complaints are acknowledged within 7 working days.
- Recorded in the official Grievance Register with date, nature of issue, and assigned handler.
## Step 2: Preliminary Assessment
- The CRC assesses urgency, risk level, and required course of action.
- Immediate hazards or severe violations are escalated without delay.
## Step 3: Investigation
- Conducted impartially and confidentially.
- Includes evidence collection, interviews, and review of relevant documents.
## Step 4: Recommendation & Action
- Findings are documented.
- Corrective and preventive actions are recommended to HR/Management.
## Step 5: Closure & Documentation
- Complainant is informed of the outcome (unless anonymous).
- Case is formally closed with records maintained for audit and review.
## Protection From Retaliation
Alchem enforces a strict zero-tolerance policy against retaliation.
No employee shall face adverse consequences for:
- Raising a concern in good faith
- Participating as a witness
- Supporting the investigation process
Any form of retaliation is treated as a serious policy violation.
## Confidentiality Assurance
All grievances and investigations are handled confidentially.
Information shared is restricted strictly on a need-to-know basis.
Any breach of confidentiality may result in disciplinary action.
## Remediation Measures
Corrective and preventive actions may include:
- Counselling or coaching
- Targeted training for departments or individuals
- Disciplinary action, including suspension or termination
- Policy revision or process strengthening
- Workplace improvements
- Safety enhancements
- Support services for affected individuals
## Monitoring, Reporting & Continuous Improvement
- The CRC periodically reviews grievance trends to identify systemic concerns.
- Annual trend analysis informs policy updates, training, and risk mitigation.
- The mechanism is reviewed every year, or earlier as required, to ensure ongoing relevance and effectiveness.

- Use of unauthorized subcontractors
- Any form of child labour or forced labour
- Safety or wage violations among vendors and contractors
## Types of Remediation Actions
[table]
| Remediation Type | Examples |
| Restorative Measures | Reinstating employees, compensating wage losses, rectifying denied entitlements, |
| Disciplinary Actions | Retraining, written warnings, suspension, removal from duty, termination of resp |
| Systemic Improvements | Policy updates, refreshed SOPs, targeted training, engineering controls, stronge |
| Supportive Actions | Counselling, mediation, medical support, temporary reassignment, protective tran |
## Stakeholder Engagement
- Affected employees are consulted before finalizing remediation actions.
- Worker committees or welfare representatives may participate in collective cases.
- Special consideration is provided to contract workers, migrant workers, female employees, and vulnerable groups.
- External stakeholders may be engaged when a grievance involves third-party service providers.
## Time-Bound Resolution
- Immediate relief for serious grievances is provided within 48 hours of case confirmation.
- Comprehensive remediation actions are implemented within 30 days, unless justified in writing.
- Follow-up assessments occur at 60–90 days to evaluate effectiveness and ensure no recurrence.
## Documentation & Confidentiality
- All grievances and remediation actions are recorded in the Grievance Register.
- Case files, investigation records, and CAPA documentation are securely maintained.
- Confidentiality is protected except when disclosure is legally required or where consent is provided.
- Annual grievance summaries are reviewed by the Grievance Committee and Senior Management.
## Third-Party Support
Where internal capacity is insufficient, Alchem may engage:
- Independent mediators or facilitators
- Legal advisors for complex or statutory matters
- External EHS experts or compliance consultants
- NGOs or social auditors for community-related or supply chain remediation
Such engagement ensures fairness, impartiality, and adherence to industry best practices.
## Monitoring & Evaluation
Remediation effectiveness is assessed through:
- Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): recurrence rate, closure timelines, resolution quality, employee satisfaction.
- Feedback tools: anonymous surveys, worker forums, interviews.
- Audit results: internal audits, third-party assessments, customer compliance audits.
- Trend analysis to identify systemic gaps and strengthen policies or SOPs.
## Review Mechanism
At Alchem International Private Limited, this Handbook is treated as a living document that reflects our values, compliance obligations, and operational excellence standards. To ensure accuracy and alignment with legal, regulatory, and ESG requirements, the Handbook undergoes a structured review led by HR, in collaboration with Compliance, Legal, and Senior Management.
The handbook is reviewed to ensure it remains:
- Compliant with applicable labour laws, ILO principles, and global customer requirements
- Aligned with Alchem’s ethical and operational standards
- Responsive to employee feedback and emerging risks
- Consistent with best practices in chemical manufacturing and international ESG expectations
The Handbook is formally reviewed once every year, or earlier when significant legal or policy changes occur. Updated versions are communicated to all employees through digital and printed formats.
